plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on upright stems above broad, blue-green leaves. Hundreds of cultivars exist, ranging from single early types to ruffled parrot and fringed forms. In the Netherlands, fields of tulips are at or just past peak bloom in early May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring (April to early May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, temperate Europe, North America; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs became so valuable in the Netherlands that single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house during 'Tulip Mania'.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with heart-shaped leaves and dense, cone-shaped clusters of intensely fragrant flowers. Lilacs reach peak bloom in many temperate regions in early to mid May and are a staple of cottage gardens and old homesteads.
plants.location: Northeastern United States, Canada, Europe; native to the Balkan Peninsula
plants.funFact: Lilacs are members of the olive family (Oleaceae), and some old plants have survived for over a century at abandoned homesites.

plants.name: Hyacinthoides non-scripta
plants.description: A bulbous woodland perennial that carpets forest floors with nodding, bell-shaped, sweetly scented flowers all arching to one side of the stem. Ancient woodlands in the British Isles are at their peak in early May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May)
plants.funFact: Britain is home to about half of the world's population of wild bluebells, and it is illegal to dig up wild bulbs for sale there.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Northern Hemisphere subtropics, such as parts of Mexico, Florida, and southern California, it starts blooming in May. In Australia and South Africa it blooms in spring around October to November, so early May bloom is typical of the north.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June)
plants.location: Subtropical regions worldwide, including Mexico City, southern California, and Florida; native to South America
plants.funFact: Fallen jacaranda blossoms create purple carpets on streets, and in some places a flower landing on your head is said to bring good luck.
